newsitem.title: USA: MHC says still no reply from Chateau.
newsitem.headline: MHC says still no reply from Chateau.

text.p: Manufactured Home Communities Inc said Tuesday it has yet to receive a response from Chateau Properties Inc after launching a tender offer of $26 a share for the company on September 4.
By law, Chateau, a Michigan-based mobile home park operator, is required to respond to MHC, a Chicago company run by investor Sam Zell, within 10 business days.
MHC spokeswoman Cindy McHugh said the company had received no word from Chateau.
Analysts said Chateau might be considering a self-tender of $27 a share, sponsored by Chateau chairman John Boll.
"I really think that John Boll is going to take a serious look at taking this baby private if he can line up the financing to offer $27 a share," said William Acheson, a Smith Barney analyst.
"He wants to maintain control, and there is a lot of ego involved here," Acheson said. "If he can make the $27 he is keeping his fiduciary duty."
Chateau officials did not return telephone calls.
BT Securities analyst Kevin Comer said a $27 a share offer by Boll would be feasible in the debt markets only if the break-up fee from a previously agreed merger with ROC Communities Inc is small.
"If the break-up fee turns out to be $10 million, then that price of $27 would drop to somewhat closer to $26 or just north," Comer said.

ROC, based in Englewood, Colorado, and Chateau agreed to merge in July. Last month Chateau said the break-up fee is "customary" and "not a small number" but would not specify how much. ROC could not be reached for comment.

Michigan-based Sun Communities Inc chief executive officer Gary Shiffman said his company has not heard back from Chateau either. It proposed a stock-swap merger last month and last week said it would also be willing to offer a cash alternative.
